checks.evidence: Rows cover deterministic mapping, leave-dataset-out mapping, profile-spec composition, rank-feature ablation, boundary backends, and boundary profile patches.
The audit preserves mapping coarsening, simple-field baseline, and inspection-cost counterpoints.
Learned boundary backend beats the best simple baseline on 4/5 rows, leaving explicit counterpoints.
All inputs are tracked artifacts or current paper/docs; this script only synthesizes existing results.
Evaluation ledger and paper drafts mention R366's scoped field-derivation role.
The paper keeps mapping/tagging/boundary outputs as operation fields folded into operation stacks.

claim: Operation-field derivation mechanisms can improve aggregation and localization when folded through operation stacks, with scoped suitability counterpoints.

mechanism_rows.counterpoint: It deliberately coarsens action labels: action->phase V-measure 0.9343->0.7416 and adjacent phase/action boundary F1 0.9677->0.7774.
mechanism_rows.evidence: Held-out mapping over 3990 operations reduces unique stacks 284->209 and improves compression 14.049->19.091; dataset->task V-measure 0.8374->0.8531.
mechanism_rows.paper_claim: Mappings are first-class field derivations for semantic aggregation, not proof of fine-grained boundary recovery.

mechanism_rows.counterpoint: Mean task/dataset V-measure is unchanged at 0.7778; some datasets are already well structured and do not benefit.
mechanism_rows.evidence: Across 9 held-out datasets / 13265 operations, mapped stacks reduce stack count on 6/9 datasets, never increase it (0 negative), and yield 1162.005 weighted stack reduction per 1k ops.
mechanism_rows.paper_claim: Mapping rules generalize as conservative compression/normalization rules, not as a universal semantic parser.

mechanism_rows.counterpoint: Depth is objective-dependent: 3/6 tasks choose different stack depths for AP and first-positive work.
mechanism_rows.evidence: 12 profile-spec variants compose operation files, predicates, operation rank rules, rule-score ranking, and explicit stack depth; 12/12 are prompt/session-frame free. AP improves versus width in 9/12 variants and first-positive work in 10/12.
mechanism_rows.mechanism: profile-spec composition of mappings, predicates, rank rules, and stack depth
mechanism_rows.paper_claim: The configurable view surface is the operation-stack query itself, not hard-coded prompt/session/span boundaries.

mechanism_rows.counterpoint: It also finds 3 misleading feature rows, including OSWorld input-phase and SATraj loop-like cases.
mechanism_rows.evidence: Leave-one-feature ablation identifies 7 critical feature rows across safety, looping, side-effect, and step-quality tasks. Examples include success, loop-like, write-action, and failure fields.
mechanism_rows.paper_claim: Actionability comes from naming useful and harmful operation fields, not from selecting one universal ranker.

mechanism_rows.counterpoint: 1/5 rows remain counterpoints; AgentRewardBench looping is better explained by repeat_signal_change than the learned backend.
mechanism_rows.evidence: Boundary backends beat the best simple baseline on 4/5 tested rows; OSWorld-Human R297 reaches F1 0.7735 versus best baseline 0.7090, and R299 also improves AgentNet quality-state boundaries.
mechanism_rows.paper_claim: Boundary detectors are optional supervised field derivation backends with suitability checks, not automatic intent discovery.

mechanism_rows.counterpoint: Inspection-cost metrics are mixed: top-5 work changes by +0.0813 and first-positive work by +0.1581.
mechanism_rows.evidence: On held-out OSWorld-Human, learned-boundary fields improve AP 0.2402->0.2583, reduce groups 108->74, and raise top-5 recall by 0.1111.
mechanism_rows.paper_claim: Derived fields can repair a rejected visible profile patch, while preserving Pareto-tradeoff wording.
